beats.narration_text: Namaste — this is Liam, in for Komal. This is Madison's weekly update. Madison is building a new Intelligence Agents layer: detect inauthentic Instagram engagement. Bots, fake followers, fake likes, fake comments. Two questions, not one.

beats.narration_text: The problem they named. A brand deciding whether to invest in an influencer has no easy way to check if that audience is real. Large companies can buy proprietary vetting. Smaller brands, independent creators, and nonprofits — the groups Humanitarians AI exists to support — cannot. Spend can go to a partnership built on fake engagement, with no way to catch it beforehand.

shot.prompt: Drawn two-card plate: enterprise can buy a desk / Madison's people cannot.

qc.sparse_reason: Two-card teaching plate; cream interiors are the layout, not missing type.

beats.narration_text: So they are building an explainable trust signal. Not a black-box verdict. A risk score with visible reasoning. It takes an account's profile and engagement data, and it answers two things: how likely the account itself is fake, and separately, how likely the likes and comments on a given post are fake. That sits next to the scraping they already have for social research.

shot.prompt: Drawn two-card plate: account fake-risk / post engagement fake-risk.

qc.sparse_reason: Two-card teaching plate; cream interiors are the layout, not missing type.

beats.narration_text: How it differs from desks they reviewed. HypeAuditor, Modash, CreatorIQ: fraud at the account level. One score from account-wide stats. Rule-based thresholds, not a trained, validated model. Madison's first difference: train a classifier on TwiBot-20, a labeled benchmark with known real versus bot, so they can measure performance instead of guessing a cutoff.

shot.prompt: Drawn two-card plate: reviewed desks as account-level rules / Madison trains on TwiBot-20 plus a second layer.

beats.narration_text: Second difference: the post. They separately ask whether the likes and comments look authentic, even if the account posting looks authentic. In their competitive reading, none of those tools appear to offer that second layer. Appear is not a census of every product.

props.caption: A second layer on the post is not a product in someone's hands.
